budget_unit: B and c_d are in units of c0 under both conventions (lead decisions L15 (3)): under C-full the unit is 1 FRE = 2,934 s, the wave-0a job slot, fixed at W1-P and never re-estimated (LW-16); after O-ext a C-full full run holds 868 greedy answers (468 + the 400 PHTest prompts) and so costs more than 1 FRE (LN-33; the predictions print costs_in_c0.full_run); under C-lean the unit is the measured lean job c0, which holds the 500-prompt over-refusal bank (LN-07; references draft LQ31). Predictions are curves in c_d/c0; the measured c0 only places a result on them (U3 (a))

C-full.source: stage-1 pre-registration DRAFT rev 2 (9ff29fc1) section 10.2 table (wave-0a ledgers, cost records only; Gate B values, named for REQ-21 (m))
C-full.stages: training 219.7 s = the median training of R_1-R_3; evaluation 2,623.2 s = the per-stage medians of greedy generation (1,694), sampled generation (638), Qwen3Guard (177), harm scores (103) and the task-loss pass (11.2) of the wave-0a jobs (468 greedy prompts: the dev 100 over-refusal prompts among them); setup 91.1 s = the rest of the job slot (load, tokenize, edit, ARC, verification); after O-ext the 400 PHTest prompts add 400 x (1,694 + 80) / 468 = 1,516.2 s to the evaluation (o_bank; LN-33), so a full run is 4,450.2 s = 1.517 FRE; a psi-trial scales the evaluation, a phi-trial the training
C-full.unit: 1 FRE = 2,934 s, the median job slot of the three wave-0a R arms (references draft LQ25; fixed at the W1-P commit, never re-estimated; LW-16); C-full holds every greedy evaluation answer, 868 after O-ext (LN-33)

C-lean.contents_rule: LQ27 (a) is the default (lead reading; [USER] if the lead reads it as a change to PLAN-S:202, then (b) is in force)
C-lean.source: references DRAFT rev 2 (5835caae) sections C.5-C.6 (E; the c0 job measures the real value); LN-07: C-lean holds the 500-prompt bank (o_bank)

a.stages: evaluation = 200 harm prompts x 1 sampled answer with its guard (245 s) + the task-loss pass (11 s) + the 100 greedy over-refusal answers (362 s) and their guard (17 s); after O-ext the 400 PHTest prompts add 1,516.2 s (o_bank; LN-07), so the lean evaluation is 2,151.2 s
a.unit: c0 = the lean job (LQ29: a cold start, the full training of an R arm, exactly this lean evaluation): 870 s on the dev 100, 2,386.2 s (0.813 FRE) with the 500-prompt bank (LN-07)

b.stages: the screen's O and L come at their full-evaluation cost (362 + 17 + 11 = 390 s on the dev 100; with the 500-prompt bank 390 + 1,516.2 = 1,906.2 s), paid by every full run
b.unit: c0 = 480 s (PLAN-S:202 as written: training plus 200 harm prompts x 1 sample)

diagnostic.rule: pays c_d out of B; if c_d > B it cannot run and the policy picks keep; if B - c_d < 2 it picks keep (lead decisions L15 (3)); else it keeps the k options with the highest scores (ties by the sealed tie order) and keep, which top-k never drops (L15 (2)), and runs the cell's frozen runs-only rule on them in the sealed tie order with budget B - c_d; bisection becomes halving (L15 (8))

limits.source: O(theta0) = 17/100 (Gate A untuned unit, the dev 100 at the Gate A cap): a planning value for the 500-prompt bank (LN-10, X-3: theta0's measured level on the 500 never enters the frozen predictions); tau_O grid (FOCUS 8 Oct); tau_L = 2 sqrt(2) s from tau_l_check.out.json (d822ba18), lead decisions addendum (11477648) L16

category.note: the 8 Gate B units (removal of one unit's 600 rows); keep = a0 at Gate A seeds 1101-1103; option ids are the Dolly category names (a replay maps the unit ids onto them)

llama_category.note: Llama's Gate B-lite menu: the same 8 units; OLMo-calibrated (no Llama measurement is an input; Llama note section 15 item 2)

method.note: the stage-1 primary arms; keep = a0 1101-1106; an object of the spec only (REQ-18 predicts the category and planted menus)

name: selector_spec

o_bank.cap: priced at the full generation cap (planning, E): ADD-9's cap branch is chosen later by W1-18; under the 128-token branch the PHTest answers cost less (UNVERIFIED PHTest answer lengths)
o_bank.rule: each convention names the over-refusal prompts its evaluation holds (o_prompts: the dev 100, or the 500-prompt bank after O-ext); the prompts beyond the dev 100 add their greedy answer and its guard to every full run at greedy_s_per_prompt + guard_s_per_answer, in the convention's evaluation (scaled by psi) or, under C-lean (b), in the screen's passes that every full run pays (o_part); the screen's O prompt part uses the same count (screen.o_prompt_sd_source)
o_bank.source: REV3 section 10.2 (wave-0a R arms, cost records only; Gate B values named for REQ-21 (m)): the median greedy generation 1,694 s and the median guard of the greedy answers 80 s, each over the 468 prompts of the ledgers' generate and guard stages; LN-33 and LN-07 (about 400 x 3.6 s = 1,450 s of greedy answers at the full cap; the guard of those answers is added here, 68.4 s)

option_cost_rule: every option's full run costs one full run of the convention's cost model (cost_fre 1.0; the name dates from when a C-full full run was 1 FRE; after O-ext it is 1.517 FRE, printed as costs_in_c0.full_run): the convention's cost model prices every trial, and menu_from refuses another value (a per-option cost is not built; verifier N-3)

pick.rule: among the options with at least 2 full-run seeds that pass the screen: the largest shrunk estimate of G = mean U of keep's seeds - mean full-run U of the option; a tie goes to the raw estimate, then to the sealed tie order; keep unless the best shrunk estimate is above 0 (a tie with keep goes to keep). Seeds are not paired: the pick models a practitioner's selection rule, which need not follow the study's analysis model (LN-11; UW-02 replaced PLAN-S:102 for the study's analysis, not for this rule)

planted_geometry.note: the planted corpus as ADD L12 builds it with no near-duplicate pairs: 8 units x 4 quartiles of 150 rows x 4 quarters of 37, 38, 37, 38 rows; the plant's 37 rows replace a 37-row leaf

psi_subsample.rule: a psi-trial replayed from saved labels uses the sealed sample of round(psi x n) harm prompts of that (option, seed index), parts (option id, seed index, psi written as %g); each psi level is its own sample (the simulation's model gives each psi level its own subsample deviation)

requirement: REQ-16 (brief rev 1 (12cbf463)); lead decisions addendum (11477648) L15 (2), (3), (8), L16; W1 builder extract rev 2 (18b81b26) W1-13; lead ruling 17 Oct 2026 15:18 UTC (addendum section 10, 995e5114) adopting lead-rulings-needed.md (9c447704): LN-10, LN-11, LN-29, LN-07, LN-33, LN-20; REV3 section 7.4 (557413e4); ledger X-1 to X-4

bisection.rule: nested menus only: from the root of the binary tree over the cells in nesting order, run t screen trials (seeds 0..t-1) on both halves of the current group and follow the half with the lower mean U (a tie follows the left half); the leaf reached gets 2 full-run seeds; t = the largest value whose descent and promotion cost at most B; the rest buys more seeds for the leaf. A group trial removes every cell of the group; its true effect is the sum of its cells' effects (additivity, an assumption)

halving.rule: rungs: the screen trial, the psi ladder of the same trained model (seed 0), then one more full-run seed per rung; ceil(n/2) options go on after each rung, until one option holds at least 2 full-run seeds; n_1 = the largest number of available options whose whole schedule costs at most B; the rest buys more full-run seeds for the options that hold 2 or more, round robin in rank order

one_shot.rule: screen n_s = min(available, floor((B - c_promote) / c_screen)) options in the sealed tie order with one trial each at the screen fidelity (seed 0); give the n_f = min(n_s, finalists, floor((B - n_s c_screen) / c_promote)) best 2 full-run seeds; spend the rest on more full-run seeds for them, round robin in rank order (at most max_seeds per option). The cap keeps the rule's E[G] from falling as B grows (without it, more budget spread 2 seeds over more finalists)

saved_labels.rule: per option and seed index: per-prompt Unsafe shares (u_prompts), per-prompt refusal flags (o_prompts), per-row task losses (l_rows); keep and the optional R arm (reference_r) the same; samples_per_prompt (top level) = the options' sampled answers per harm prompt, which must equal the convention's (C-full 3, C-lean 1), and keep.samples_per_prompt = C-full's 3 (keep's seeds are C-full runs at any convention); a replay of labels with another count refuses, so the replay has the model's sampling variance (verifier S-8; a lean replay of full evaluations would need a sealed 1-of-3 sample per prompt and a new registry key, not built). Version 2 adds the two counts

screen.coherence_rule: an option that fails the arm-pooled answers-end bar is infeasible (Draft B section F item 6); the simulation's default is that no option fails
screen.l_item_sd_note: planning value (E) from the Gate A a0 task-row tables (query_loss.jsonl of a0 1101-1103 at e1, 200 rows, SHA-256 a539638f, 2f73f77c, eba94724; notes/l_item_sd_check.py of the Part E rev-2 hand-over): the mean over the 3 seed pairs of the paired per-row SE of a single-seed L contrast against an a0 seed, SD_p(L(j, p) - L(j', p)) / sqrt(200) = 2.71, 2.61 and 3.09 x 1e-3 nats, the same construction as O's planning value (CK-3 4.2: the paired per-prompt SE against the screen's reference). The a0 tables cannot identify an option x row interaction; the value plans one of the size of a seed-to-seed row deviation. The smaller alternative sqrt(MS_E / 200) = 0.001989 nats (the row x seed interaction alone, 398 df) is recorded in the hand-over
screen.o_error_model_note: it must equal REQ-19's u8_decider (W1-13 row 2; K4)
screen.o_prompt_sd_source: CK-3 section 4.2 (Gate A: the paired per-prompt SE of O(a0 seed) - O(untuned) is 4.16, 4.22 and 3.91 pp at the dev 100 prompts; their mean, rounded); seeds do not shrink it. It is the dev-100 value: the screen and the model use it x sqrt(100 / o_prompts) at the convention's over-refusal prompts, 4.1 x sqrt(1/5) = 1.834 pp at the 500-prompt bank (LW-12, LN-10, X-3: planning values, assuming PHTest prompts behave like dev prompts)
screen.se_form_rule: hb (LW-13 with LN-20; in force, LN-10): O against theta0: the option's mean full-run O; seed part = the sample variance (ddof 1) of its own full-run O values / n (n - 1 df); item part = the prompt part under prompts_random (REC (e) rule 9's theta0 form). L against the reference arm: the paired mean of L(option, j) - L(reference, j) over the common seed indices (the option's full-run seeds below the reference's seed count); seed part = the sample variance (ddof 1) of those differences / J (J - 1 df); item part = l_item_sd_nats squared (REC (e) rule 9's cross-cluster form; the method menu's add options take the same paired form, since a two-arm screen cannot fit HB-C). Each bound = estimate + t_q(df) sqrt(seed + item), q = upper_quantile, df by Satterthwaite with the item part a known planning constant (one estimate, one SE, one df: REC (c) rule 4); fewer than 2 seeds: no bound, not feasible. With keep's 3 seeds the paired L form has at most 2 df whatever the option's seed count. hb_unpaired (a switch, the builder's alternative; the lead rules): O as hb; L = the option's mean over all its full-run seeds - the reference's mean over all its seeds, seed part = the option's own sample variance / n + the reference's own sample variance / its seed count, Welch-Satterthwaite df, the same item part (the seed part of the rev-1 hb form, with the t quantile). pooled_residuals (lead decisions L16; the fallback): seed part = the pooled within-option variance of the full runs (options with 2 or more seeds and the comparison arm's seeds) / n, normal quantile; O adds the prompt part under prompts_random
screen.tau_l_reference_note: a0 (PLAN-S:124; LW-07 decided a0, LN-11); r = the dose-matched random-removal arm, kept as a switch for the replay's report (W1-13 row 4). The screen uses a0; a replay reports the L upper bound against both a0 and R (R when the saved labels hold its seeds; spec.l_bounds_report). In the simulation both references give the same truth while the true L effects and R's effect are 0 (the defaults), so the simulation runs a0 only
screen.uo_reading: REQ-16's 'with the U-O noise correlation from pooled residuals' is read as: the U-O correlation enters the generative model only (simulate.py: each full run's O seed noise is correlated with its standardized U noise, rho_UO from Gate A's a0 seeds); the screen bounds O and L separately and has no U-O term. A builder reading for REQ-21 (h) (verifier S-6); if the lead reads it as a screen rule (for example an O bound conditional on the U estimate), that rule is built behind a switch
screen.upper_quantile_reading: the upper end of the two-sided 90% interval (one-sided 95%), RB R1.2 and Draft B; Draft A proposes 0.90 (W1-13 row 1); REQ-21 (h) records the reading

shrinkage.method: normal-normal empirical Bayes, method of moments, per replicate over every option with at least one full-run seed: mu = their mean estimate, tau^2 = max(0, their variance (ddof 1) - their mean sampling variance), shrunk = mu + tau^2 / (tau^2 + v)(estimate - mu); v = the pooled U residual variance x (1/n + 1/J_keep)

ties.rule: the sealed order of a menu's option ids other than keep (sorted, then shuffled by the registry key); it is the visiting order of every rule and breaks every tie between options; a tie with keep goes to keep

phi_switch.note: phi < 1 trials (part training) exist neither on OLMo's category menu nor on Llama (Llama note section 15 item 3) and save at most 7.5% of a unit under C-full, so the default grid is {1}; with the switch the screen may run at phi = 0.5

trials.rule: a trial costs (setup + phi x training + psi x evaluation) / c0; raising psi of a trained model from a to b costs (b - a) x evaluation / c0; a full run is phi = psi = 1
